title: late-sprint-latency-fossils-kernel-notes-2026-06-22
content:
Weekly standup + deep-dive notes (late sprint scramble)

Context / why this doc exists:
- During last week's microkernel rollout we saw several reappearing high-tail latency traces (what I'm calling 'latency fossils') that we thought were mitigated months ago. This doc captures the standup capture, quick triage, experiments run, and immediate action items. Intentionally rough — notes to self + triage log.

Meeting 2026-06-22 10:30am PT — attendees: Priya, Jamal, Liang, Ava, Samir, oncall
- Quick recap: p95 stable, p99 moved from ~420ms -> ~940ms after kernel v2.14.1. Spike frequency ~ 0.6% of requests.
- Observed pattern: majority of traces correlate with concurrent cold-KV evictions + batch coalescer handoff. Services: hosted-api route /v1/generate (medium-length sequences).
- Hypothesis 1 (H1): kernel micro-optim changed reorderer handshake timing, exposing a race that lets a stale KV slot be double-evicted causing large blocking on allocator.
- Hypothesis 2 (H2): coalescer TTL change from 4s->1s (perf tweak) increases eviction churn, causing extra prefill work and long tails during bursty arrival windows.
- Hypothesis 3 (H3): thermal throttling + longer kernel slot reclamation when GPU warms up on pods with older firmware.

Quick evidence pulled during meeting:
- Sampled 200 p99 traces, flagged 127 with a common stack: kernel::queue_wait -> kv::evict_sync -> allocator::global_lock.
- Metric snapshot (last 72h): eviction_count/day +240%, average coalescer TTL decreased as expected.
- Microbenchmark: synthetic burst test against v2.14.1 shows p99 bloat only when coalescer concurrency > 6 and eviction rate > 15/s.

Experiments run (immediate, on-call):
1) Revert coalescer TTL to 4s on a small canary: rolled to 3 pods on cluster a. Observed p99 drop to ~480ms on that canary within 20 minutes. (Owner: Jamal)
2) Applied kernel patch (PR 1287) that adds a timeout to the reorderer handshake and extra asserts. Deployed to canary pool. No immediate crash, but p99 improved marginally. (Owner: Liang)
3) Forced GC/eviction-reservation change (allocator backoff 200ms -> 50ms) on staging to see contention changes; caused increased median but lowered p99 in synthetic. (Owner: Ava)

Notes / odd behaviors:
- We found traces where eviction path took 2.1s due to blocking on a per-allocator freelist drain. That code path used to be ~80ms historically.
- A small subset of requests (heavy multi-turn chat with embedding lookup + long output) amplify the effect. Not a single-route issue, but RT-features combine to create worst-case.
- Logs show an intermittent log line: "kv: shadow-evict requested on slot X but slot->owner == NULL" — likely timing window between owner release and eviction handler.

Decisions (temporary):
- Roll TTL back to 4s on both canary and additional 6 pods for the next 24h while we gather metrics (Jamal).
- Keep kernel PR 1287 in canary and add verbose tracing for handshake paths (Liang).
- Disable aggressive allocator backoff change in production for now; only experiment on staging (Ava).

Action items (short term):
- Jamal: expand TTL rollback to additional canaries, capture p50/p95/p99 and eviction_rate every 5m for 24h. Create short dashboard grain for triangle view (eviction_count / p99 / coalescer_concurrency). Due: 2026-06-23 EOD.
- Liang: add flamegraph sampling for the allocator path in PR1287, push new build with extra logs and a feature flag to toggle handshake assert tracing. Due: 2026-06-24 morning.
- Ava: run controlled synthetic bursts across kernel versions (v2.13.x, v2.14.0, v2.14.1) and produce a CSV of p50/p95/p99 for coalescer_concurrency set {2,4,8,12}. Due: 2026-06-25.
- Priya: write a short postmortem draft if rollback shows improvement; otherwise escalate to SRE/firmware. Due: 2026-06-26.

TODOs (investigation deeper):
- Reproduce the "slot->owner == NULL" window with a deterministic test harness. Hypothesis: reorderer handshake can run concurrently with slot release in specific timing.
- Confirm whether mixed-firmware nodes correlate with incidents (Samir to pull node metadata / firmware versions).
- Evaluate whether we can apply a lightweight per-slot CAS to prevent double-evict. Perf impact unknown.

Longer-term ideas (brainstorm, rough):
- Consider a soft-eviction queue: mark slots as "pending-evict" and let coalescer drain with upper bound. Avoid hard sync evict during heavy bursts.
- Revisit coalescer backoff strategy: tune based on per-route seq-length distribution (we can be route-aware).
- Add a small KV shadow cache keyed by session id for multi-turn flows (trade memory for fewer evictions).

Unresolved questions:
- Is this purely kernel timing + coalescer TTL, or is there an external contributor (e.g., deployment churn, autoscaler flaps)? Need autoscaler logs correlation.
- Why did this pattern show up only after v2.14.1 rollout even though coalescer TTL was previously tested in canary? Was canary traffic different in shape?

Raw snippets pulled during triage (redacted):
- stack: kernel::queue_wait -> kv::evict_sync -> allocator::global_lock -> nv_mem::sync_copy
- sample log: [2026-06-22T09:18:41Z] WARN kv: shadow-evict requested on slot 0xafa23d but slot->owner == NULL
- metric spike: eviction_rate 0.23 -> 3.2 evictions/s during burst window

Meeting quick retro/notes to self:
- We keep seeing classes of regressions that are not full regressions but amplify tail. For oncall, prefer conservative opt-in for short TTL/async evict changes.
- Instrumentation is still the pace-limiter. Add lightweight per-path timing tags in next build so we can immediately attribute delays to either kernel handshake, kv eviction, or allocator contention.

Appendix (links & references):
- PR 1287: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1287
- Jira INF-3421: spike to reproduce eviction race
- Jira INF-3499: coalescer TTL experiment and rollout notes

End notes:
- If rollback (TTL=4s) shows stable p99 for 12h, we'll schedule a full revert for the cluster. If not, escalate to SRE + firmware triage.
- Keep this doc as the ephemeral triage log; I'll turn into a short postmortem if we have a clear root cause.

---
Notes to self: this felt different from past eviction issues because of the allocator freelist drain exploding latencies. Revisit allocator freelist design (Samir + Liang pairing session next week).
